source.title: Alice: Proactive Learning with Teacher's Demonstrations for Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Shu-Jin Wu; Cheng Qian; Yi R. Fung; P. Liang; Heng Ji

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates weak-to-strong fine-tuning and an enhanced supervision method on new model families and tasks, but reports accuracy comparisons rather than Burns et al.'s PGR measure.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports weak-model, original W2SG, Alice, and strong-model accuracies. Rows below capture the original W2SG Q-A and Q-CoT-A comparisons with weak performance, Alice versus Q-CoT-A, and Table 2's two ablations. Other Table 2 variants (Multi-teacher, Mix-teacher, Cross-model, and Cross-model-Cascade) and Table 3's separate direct-versus-cascade comparisons are not included; the 60-row limit was not reached, but they are additional method configurations rather than necessary for the basic and method-gain verdicts. The paper does not calculate PGR.
record.test_reason: The study runs original W2SG (teacher-label fine-tuning in Q-A and Q-CoT-A formats) on Qwen 2.5 and Llama pairs across four NLP tasks, comparing it to weak and strong references (V1, V3). It also tests a new training change, Alice, against naive W2SG (V2). It reports accuracy, not PGR, but Table 1 gives weak, student and strong values, so PGR can be computed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right: the authors conclude that Alice (uncertainty-informed proactive student demonstrations) and cascade Alice improve W2SG, with Alice often beating strong models trained on gold labels. However, their claim that original W2SG only partly bridges the weak-strong gap is contradicted by their own Table 1 in several cells, where Q-CoT-A W2SG exceeds the strong reference (Qwen 3B HotpotQA/TriviaQA, Llama 3B HotpotQA/TriviaQA, Llama 8B HotpotQA).
record.recipe_differences: The original W2SG baseline directly fine-tunes students on teacher-generated answers, also tested with generated or annotated chain-of-thought. Alice adds teacher uncertainty elicitation and the student's own zero-shot answer to construct refined demonstrations; cascade Alice adds intermediate teacher-student stages. The paper reports accuracy, not PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dataset/task and label format: Q-A results often fall below weak performance, while Q-CoT-A results exceed it in all reported conditions. Alice is below Q-CoT-A for Llama HotpotQA; ablations show lower results without cascade or teacher uncertainty.
record.problems: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. PGR is not calculated, and accuracy comparisons do not quantify the share of the weak-to-strong gap recovered. The experiments cover four datasets and two model families; the authors also note reliance on eliciting uncertainty, a single-turn setup, and a two-stage cascade.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2's Multi-teacher, Mix-teacher, Cross-model, and Cross-model-Cascade results are not extracted. Table 3's additional original-W2SG direct-versus-cascade and Alice direct-versus-cascade comparisons are also omitted. These are further settings beyond the selected 56 rows.

untested.parts: PGR is not computed by the authors, although it is computable from Table 1. The actual supervisor's accuracy is never reported.
Auxiliary confidence loss and loss variants. Ensembling is only touched on via the Multi-teacher and Mix-teacher variants of Alice.
Chess and reward modelling tasks; representational predictors of PGR; systematic size scaling beyond two pairs per family.

missing.what: Strong-ceiling accuracies (strong model fine-tuned on gold labels) for every pair and dataset, needed to compute PGR. Q-CoT-A W2SG exceeds this ceiling in several knowledge cells, e.g. Qwen 3B HotpotQA 22.21 vs 14.76, giving PGR>1 and suggesting the ceiling is not comparable (Q-A gold).

Original W2SG 3B->7B direct vs 1.5B->7B cascade (28.55/61.87/69.04/84.65 vs 26.31/57.19/67.53/83.36): cascading naive W2SG does not help. Also Alice w/o cascade (direct 1.5B->7B) vs original W2SG Q-CoT-A 1.5B->7B, a cleaner V2 comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Key caveats: (1) The weak and strong references are models fine-tuned on gold labels from the latter half of the training set, not the actual teacher, and use Q-A format except on GSM8K. Comparisons with CoT-trained students are therefore format-confounded, and PGR computed from these references can exceed 1. (2) Alice's supervision pipeline uses Qwen2.5-70B-Instruct to write teacher uncertainty statements and the student's own zero-shot answers, so it is not purely weak supervision. (3) No error bars or seeds are reported. (4) The Table 1 header says 'Qwen 2.5 1B to 7B', presumably meaning 1.5B. (5) The ablation rows r49-r56 compare Alice with itself and are relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports student and weak-model accuracies for two original-W2SG label formats, but does not calculate PGR or compare it to the strong-model ceiling using the PGR formula.
Tests Alice and ablations; does not test auxiliary confidence losses or loss variants. Some additional teacher-combination and cross-model conditions are reported but not extracted as rows.
Varies model pairs and task datasets and compares some supervision configurations. Does not analyze internal representations or predictors of PGR, and does not report PGR.
Does not systematically test exploitation of supervisor-checking limits, distribution shift, or effects of teacher/student error similarity.
No theoretical conditions for a student necessarily beating its supervisor are tested or derived.
Experiments are on language tasks, not vision or other non-language modalities.
